A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EmbodMocap and contain readable main text and supplementary Sections 9–13. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original capture evaluations, loss ablations, EMDB reconstruction results, simulated interaction and tracking experiments, and real-robot demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 2–6 and the simulation and robot demonstrations.

M1.justification: The four-stage capture system, calibration and motion objectives, monocular reconstruction pipeline, and control procedures are unchanged. The added sentence introducing loss definitions does not modify the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same captured dataset, EMDB evaluation, optical-studio recordings, six interaction skills, four tracking scenes, and humanoid demonstrations. Section 13 retains 23 scenes, 104 sequences, and approximately 200,000 frames.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same GVHMR, single-view, fine-tuning, and optical-mocap comparisons. Human3R and Crisp are added only to related work, without evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The studio sample, 100/500/1000-frame comparisons, EMDB chunking and metrics, interaction success thresholds, and 3,072 tracking episodes per scene are unchanged. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The loss ablations, single-view versus dual-view analysis, fine-tuning variants, data-proportion experiments, and qualitative case studies are retained. The appendix adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: The APD uncertainty reporting in Table 5 and episode-length statistics in Table 6 are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises seed information, repeated-run reporting, or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–6 match, and the qualitative examples and findings are retained. For example, Table 4's jointly fine-tuned model remains at 82.21 WA-MPJPE, 220.65 W-MPJPE, and 1.71 RTE.

T1.justification: Equation 1 adds the view index v to trajectory notation, making explicit the existing per-view formulation. This is equivalent notation; the mathematical objectives, definitions, and supplementary derivations are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The rewritten contribution bullets foreground the framework and dataset already described in v1. The substantive claims about portable metric capture and three downstream applications remain the same, as do the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: The explanations of depth ambiguity, dual-view benefits, data scaling, and physical realism are retained. Section 7 preserves the same limitations concerning LiDAR range, moving objects, and bright lighting.

D1.justification: Implementation and capture instructions, supplementary technical details, and the project-page link are unchanged. Expanding SAI to SpectacularAI in Section 9.2 provides no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds descriptions and citations for Human3R's feed-forward reconstruction and Crisp's contact-guided Real2Sim approach. These two additions modestly expand research context without substantially restructuring the positioning.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the contribution list, makes localized wording and notation edits, adds a loss-definition signpost, and expands acknowledgments with funding and another actor. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 replaces separate subcaptions with one numbered caption. Table 3 and Figure 6 move to subsequent pages, with additional spacing and text reflow. The underlying illustrations and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer contribution framing, the Human3R and Crisp discussion, and an explicit Figure 5 caption modestly improve exposition and research context. Scientific evidence is unchanged. The gain is limited by incomplete consistency editing: Section 5.1 still says no feed-forward model exists despite the added Human3R description.
